summary: First soak check: 0 lost jobs over 12 min, no kills or restarts yet, ledger reconciles; trends not yet assessable.
body:
First soak check. There are no earlier reports, so this is the baseline. The driver run started 2026-10-10 17:00:29 UTC and was about 12 minutes old at check time (17:12:35).

Uptime and chaos: Aquifer pid 652 has been up since 17:00 (aquifer_up_s ~767 at check). Kills 0, restarts 0, no crash or panic in the logs. The chaos so far is one upstream "slow" window (17:00:34 to 17:10:34), now back to healthy. Webhook mode has been healthy throughout.

Ledger since run start (cumulative, run is new): submitted 360,435; accepted 239,064; shed_429_503 121,366; client_errors 0; completed_webhooks 239,059; failed_webhooks 0; duplicate_webhooks 0; finished_without_webhook 0; stuck_over_24h 0; lost 0; lost_within_flush_window_of_kill 0. Outstanding 5, oldest 0s. Counters reconcile: accepted = completed + outstanding (239,059 + 5 = 239,064).

Behaviour during the slow-upstream window: outstanding climbed to about 10,000 and held there (looks like a queue cap, not confirmed) while accept p99 stayed about 23-37 ms. Shedding was about 200-230 req/s with accepted about 270-300/s. E2E p99 reached about 38.5 s. After the upstream recovered at 17:10, the backlog drained within about 2 minutes (completed 666/s at 17:11, outstanding 5 by 17:12, e2e p99 back to 67.8 ms). Shedding is in proportion to the slow upstream and the 10k backlog.

Trends: not assessable yet. There are no hourly or daily summaries (the run is under one hour old), so there is no day-over-day comparison. Snapshot values at 17:12: RSS about 165 MB, heap alloc about 91 MB, goroutines 200 (1,576 at peak during the slow window), open fds 140 (peak 597), Pebble about 49 files and 200 MB, volume 9.7 GB free of 10.4 GB.

Harness health: the minute series is complete from 17:01. No generator_saturated or minutes_target_unreachable entries. No driver restart gaps. Ledger arithmetic is consistent.

Unexplained or to watch: Aquifer logs "AQUIFER_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB is not set - process memory is unbounded" at startup. RSS is currently low (about 165 MB), but the memory budget is unset, so growth under a long soak would not be capped. I am not calling this a problem yet.

Next: let the first hourly and daily summaries land, then compare RSS, heap, goroutines, fds and Pebble size across kills and the first daily ramp (04:00 UTC). Check that accept and e2e p99 in steady healthy phases hold, and that the first kill's lost_within_flush_window count stays at 0 or explains any loss. Confirm the ramp ceiling in /status/daily at 04:00 UTC.

summary: Pebble DB grew to the 800 MiB admission cap and Aquifer is rejecting jobs; 0 lost jobs so far
body:
Uptime: Aquifer pid 652 has been up since the driver run started at 17:00:29 UTC (aquifer_up_s 4667 at 18:17). Kills 0, restarts 0, last_exit empty. The first scheduled kill is still to come.

Ledger since the last report (17:12, run totals): submitted 2,442,994; accepted 1,893,072; shed_429_503 549,922; completed 1,891,934; failed_webhooks 1,030; finished_without_webhook 108; duplicates 0; lost 0; lost_within_flush_window_of_kill 0; stuck_over_24h 0. Reconciles exactly: completed + failed + finished_without_webhook + outstanding = 1,891,934 + 1,030 + 108 + 0 = accepted 1,893,072.

Expected outcomes: the webhook receiver was in errors_503 from 17:50 to 18:00, and the failures and finished-without-webhook jobs fall in that window. I am treating that as expected. Outstanding rose to about 650 during it and drained after recovery. Shedding during the 18:00 burst was in proportion.

PROBLEM: Pebble data grew with no sign of reclamation, and Aquifer has hit its DB-size admission cap. Pebble went from about 30 MB at 17:01 to 223 MB at 17:13, 536 MB at 17:31, 706 MB at 17:46 and about 840-860 MB from 18:01. That growth happened during healthy steady load with outstanding about 5. Logs now say "admission: rejecting job - db size 860263016 bytes exceeds limit 838860800 bytes" (800 MiB). Accepts were 0/s from 18:02 to 18:04 with 500/s shed. Since 18:05 accepts run about 400-430/s against 500 offered, so roughly 80-100/s are shed while the queue is nearly empty. Volume is fine (8.97 GB free). I cannot see the retention or compaction policy from the status pages, so I cannot say whether this plateaus or keeps climbing.

Trends: there is only one hourly summary (17:00 hour), so no day-over-day comparison yet. Snapshot at 18:18: RSS about 230 MB (burst peak 305 MB), heap in use about 110-160 MB. Goroutines in healthy phases were about 200 at 17:12 and 240-380 at 18:10-18:18. Open fds were about 140 at 17:12 and 260-335 now. Steady healthy e2e p99 was about 60-75 ms at 17:12-17:19, about 150-280 ms at 17:33-17:50 and about 100-140 ms at 18:11-18:18. Accept p99 went from about 40 ms to about 60-95 ms. These are all too early to call trends, and the e2e rise may be Pebble compaction load, which I have not confirmed.

Harness: the minute series is complete, minutes_target_unreachable is 0, there are no alerts, no generator_saturated entries and no driver restart gaps. The daily summary is still null; the next ramp is at 04:00 UTC on 11 Oct.

Unexplained: whether completed-job data is ever purged; why the DB grows in healthy steady load; whether the fd and goroutine levels are returning to baseline after the slow and 503 windows. I have not re-checked the memory-limit warning from the first report.

Next: (1) check whether Pebble size plateaus or keeps rising over the next hours without the cap being in play; (2) read the retention/compaction behaviour for completed jobs; (3) watch the 04:00 ramp. With the DB pinned at the cap, the ramp ceiling will reflect the cap, not throughput; (4) check lost_within_flush_window on the first kill; (5) confirm that the cap is intended.

summary: Pebble DB still growing (756 MB to 2.8 GB in 7 h, no plateau; ~16 h to fill volume at current rate); 0 lost jobs
body:

Ledger since last report (17:12 to 00:23): accepted 11,722,566 (1,893,072 at 18:19); completed 11,658,057; failed 35,355; finished_without_webhook 29,021; duplicates 9; outstanding 134. lost 0, unchanged. lost_within_flush_window_of_kill 2: jobs 243202a20cc71e77f948e94a46cb0e6d and 34e52dbe0dbd014a20a37dd98b1508be, accepted 23:18:00.469, 6 ms before the kill. Expected flush-window case. Logs for that time have rolled out of the buffer. The ledger sum is 1 above accepted; probably snapshot skew, unverified.

PROBLEM, disk: Pebble by hour: 756 MB (17:00), 1,190 (19:00), 1,567 (21:00), 2,082 (22:00), 2,364 (23:00), 2,800 MB (00:22). Files 140 to 517. It rises every hour under the same steady load. Volume has 7.0 GB free of 10.4 GB. At about 436 MB/h (21:23 to 00:22) that is roughly 16 h to full, unless something reclaims space. The 800 MiB admission cap I reported at 18:19 does not seem to apply: healthy steady minutes at 21:23, 22:03 and 00:03 show shed 0 with Pebble at 1.5 to 2.5 GB. I cannot tell whether it was raised or removed.

Steady e2e p99 200 to 350 ms (60 to 75 ms at 17:12). Healthy accept p99 86 to 121 ms. The 00:22 minute (fds 4,128, goroutines 3,914, accept p99 1.87 s) is one minute after a burst; not re-checked.

Harness: complete minute series except a 1-minute target-unreachable in the 19:00 hour. No generator_saturated, no new alerts. Driver restart gap at 19:16. The 04:00 UTC ramp has not run, so the ceiling is unknown.

Unexplained: the 19:17 process replacement; the cap; whether completed-job data is ever purged.

Next: (1) find Aquifer's Pebble retention for completed jobs and whether it runs; (2) check supervisor logs for the 19:17 replacement; (3) watch whether Pebble stops growing before free space nears 2 GB; (4) read the 04:00 ramp ceiling against cap state.

- RSS in healthy steady minutes: 210 to 240 MB, flat since 17:00.
- Healthy steady goroutines 330 to 470, and fds 437 to 503 (about 140 and 140 at 17:12). Peaks are chaos-driven. I am not calling a leak; a few more days of the same pattern will settle this.

- Watch: hourly accept and e2e p99 repeat exact values across hours (38527.34 at 17:00, 23:00 and 00:00; 373.93 at 20:00 to 22:00). That looks like coarse histogram buckets or a cumulative histogram. Worth checking the harness.

- 00:34:57: aquifer pid 776 to 652, aquifer_up_s and supervisor_up_s both reset to about 13s, no kill event, kills and restarts counters at 0. Load was paused 00:33 to 00:35. Pebble dropped from 2.7 GB to 1.8 GB across the same window. The 19:17 replacement is also unexplained. The supervisor may have restarted, but I cannot confirm.
- Logs: the buffer holds only 02:36:54 to 02:36:57, so the 02:24 kill and the 00:34 window cannot be checked. The grep parameter returns nothing, so I cannot search by term.

Next:
1. Check that the 03:17 webhook-slow backlog drains, and that lost stays 0.
2. Read the 04:00 ramp ceiling and check it against the Pebble plateau.
3. Find the supervisor logs for 00:34 and 19:17 to explain the replacements.
4. Check that Pebble stays about 1.6 to 2.0 GB across the next kills and the 36h machine restart.

summary: 0 lost jobs (unchanged). New: 37.9k accepted jobs outstanding since the 06:07 webhook-down window, not draining after 12 min of healthy webhooks.
body:
Uptime and chaos: run started 17:00:29 UTC Oct 10, about 13h20m old. Kills: 23:18:00 and 02:24:41 UTC (2 total, both in /events). Last kill was 3h56m ago, so the next one is due soon on the 3-5h cadence. Aquifer pid 716 since 02:24. No full machine restart yet. Still unexplained: the process replacements at 00:34 and 19:17 (no kill event).

Ledger since last report (03:19): accepted +5,165,136 (16,662,437 to 21,827,573); completed +5,048,196; failed +73,294; finished_without_webhook +13,084 (29,021 to 42,105, all in the 03:57 webhook-down window, expected); duplicates 13 to 13 (none new). lost 0, unchanged. lost_within_flush_window_of_kill 2, unchanged (23:18 kill, expected). Outstanding 37,893, oldest 789 s. The ledger reconciles to within 1 (completed+failed+fwh+outstanding = 21,827,574 vs accepted 21,827,573), the same snapshot skew as before.

WHAT IS NEW (warning): webhook down 06:06:57 to about 06:09. Outstanding went 4 (06:05) to 19.5k (06:07) to 41.1k (06:09). Since then, with upstream and webhooks both reported healthy, completed is about 500/s (equal to accepted), and outstanding has sat at 37.9k for 10 minutes (06:11 to 06:19). failed and fwh have not moved since 05:00. So these jobs are not lost, but they are not draining either. For comparison, the 03:57 webhook-down backlog (13.5k to 23k) stayed near 13k until about 04:15 and reached 4 by 04:29. The 04:56 upstream-down backlog cleared in about 6 min. The current backlog is larger and has lasted longer than either. I cannot see webhook retry state on the status pages.

Unexplained: at 06:09:51-52 the Aquifer log shows AccountQueue "retry N ... upstream returned 503" lines, but the driver reports upstream healthy from 05:16 onward. I cannot tell whether those 503s come from the upstream or from a stale mode. The log buffer holds only 500 lines (about 1 s), and the grep parameter returns nothing, so I cannot check further.

Trends (about 13 h, still early): Healthy-steady RSS flat at 210-277 MB at each hour end; heap 125-220 MB. Pebble hourly end 1,648 (00:00), 1,742, 1,692, 1,719, 1,817, 1,786 (05:00), now 1.87 GB. Plateau since 00:00, no growth since the 800 MiB cap question. Files 216-286. Volume free about 76%. Open fds: healthy hour ends 438-626 earlier, 497 at 05:00. Healthy goroutines 340-660. Healthy accept p99 about 80-135 ms, steady e2e p99 about 150-310 ms, flat with no clear drift. The daily ramp ceiling is 750/s (04:05 run). The 1000/s step was not sustained (873 accepted, 122 shed). It ran with about 13k of backlog carried over from 03:57, so treat it as a rough first point. No prior ceiling to compare with.

Harness: minute series complete. minutes_target_unreachable is 0 in the last 5 hours. No generator_saturated. One driver restart gap (19:16:57). Hourly summaries are landing through 05:00.

Next: (1) confirm the 06:09 backlog drains and that failed or fwh rise only after webhook retries are exhausted; (2) check whether Aquifer has a webhook retry or backoff cap that the 37.9k backlog is hitting; (3) check the next kill for lost_within_flush_window and lost; (4) find the supervisor logs for 00:34 and 19:17; (5) check the second ramp at 04:00 UTC on 12 Oct against the 750/s ceiling.

summary: 0 lost jobs; Pebble has plateaued (~1.75 GB since 00:00); unrecorded Aquifer restart at 00:34 and 9 flush-window losses at the 06:54 kill need explaining
body:
Uptime and restarts: run started 17:00:29 UTC Oct 10, about 16h15m old at check time (09:16). Kills: 23:18:00, 02:24:41 and 06:54:00 UTC (3 total, all in /events, 3h06m and 4h30m apart). No full machine restart yet (the 36h cadence falls around 05:00 UTC Oct 12). Two process replacements have no kill event: 19:17 (same window as the driver restart at 19:16:57) and 00:34:57.

Ledger since the 06:21 report: accepted +4,746,488 (21,827,573 to 26,574,061). lost 0, unchanged. lost_within_flush_window_of_kill 2 to 11: nine new jobs accepted 06:54:00.356 to .367, around the 06:54:00.349 kill (expected category, but those timestamps are after the kill event time, so the event time may be the send time; unverified). duplicates 13 to 34, all within 10 min of a restart (expected). failed +41,460 in the 07:07 to 07:16 upstream-down window (expected). finished_without_webhook +37,867, all in the 06:00 hour, matching the 37.9k backlog that sat outstanding from 06:11 and drained by 06:41. Those jobs were finished without webhook, not lost, but the outage was short (events say 10 min) and the backlog stayed outstanding about 30 min after recovery. The 06:21 report flagged this as the open question, and the counters answer it. Client errors total 73,345: about 20k per recorded kill (roughly 40 s of refused requests at 500/s, from the 06:54 minute: 133 accepted, 367 errors/s), plus 10,659 in the 00:00 hour, which has no recorded kill. Outstanding 14. Counters reconcile to within 8 (snapshot skew, unverified).

Trends (about 16 h, one day, so still early):
- Pebble: hourly end 1,648 to 1,817 MB from 00:00 to 08:00 (1,717 at 08:00, 1.75 GB now). Files 216 to 286. Volume about 77% free. The growth I flagged at 00:24 has not resumed.
- RSS: hourly end 210 to 277 MB, flat. Healthy-steady minutes 221 to 257 MB.
- Goroutines and fds: healthy-steady 340 to 660 and 420 to 610. Bursts, kills and slow windows peak at 3,000 to 4,900 goroutines and 3,000 to 4,200 fds, then return. Hour-end fds 438 to 515 at 00:00 to 02:00 and 458 to 497 at 05:00 to 07:00. Not a climb yet.
- Healthy accept p99 78 to 134 ms; steady e2e p99 115 to 373 ms. No drift since 00:00.
- Daily ramp: ceiling 750/s at 04:05 (750 sustained; 1000 gave 873 accepted and 122 shed, with about 13k carried backlog). One point only.

Harness: 180-minute series complete. minutes_target_unreachable 0 in the last 5 hours. No generator_saturated, no new alerts. Hourly summaries land through 08:00 with no gaps. The only driver restart gap is 19:16:57. Limitations: the log buffer holds about 2 seconds (500 lines ending 07:09:39), and the grep parameter returns nothing, so I cannot check the 06:54 or 00:34 windows. The e2e p99 values repeat exactly across hours (38527.34, 36692.71), which suggests coarse histogram buckets.

Unexplained: (1) the 00:34:57 process replacement with no kill event, during a load pause (00:33 to 00:35), with client errors in that hour; this could be a crash and automatic restart, but I cannot confirm it. (2) The 19:17 replacement. (3) The 06:09 AccountQueue 503 retries logged while the upstream was reported healthy.

Next: (1) supervisor logs for 00:34 and 19:17 (crash, OOM or panic?). (2) Startup time after each kill, since about 40 s of refused requests is large for a 1.8 GB Pebble. (3) Whether kill events are logged at send or at exit, to explain the post-kill accept timestamps. (4) Webhook retry budget, using the 37.9k finished-without-webhook result. (5) Fix log retention and the grep parameter. (6) The 04:00 UTC Oct 12 ramp against 750/s, and the 36h machine restart.

The e2e p99 pins at exactly 38527.34 ms in degraded minutes, which looks like a histogram ceiling, so degraded e2e is not usable. The log buffer holds about 500 lines (seconds), and grep returns nothing, so I cannot check the 14:25 job IDs or the 13:48 to 14:06 webhook backlog in the logs.

Next:
1. Webhook retry and backoff budget: why 16k to 21k jobs waited about 18 min with healthy webhooks and then ended without webhook.
2. Whether kill events are logged at send or at exit.
3. Supervisor logs for 00:34 and 19:17.
